chapter: Philadelphia, Detroit and back to Atlantic City
title: Bessie Smith in Atlantic City
summary: Wooding says Atlantic City audiences, who liked joyful or sentimental songs, did not appreciate Bessie Smith's blues.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Now, Bessie Smith was also at the Paradise around this time. But she wasn't really very well known.
Did you hear about her at all?

Well, Bessie Smith was there and she did alright with the people, but a lot of people didn't appreciate Bessie Smith. Not because Bessie Smith wasn't a singer, but because they hadn't had a touch of the Blues.

They really didn't understand the Blues. And then when anybody -- when Bessie Smith sang the Blues, the Blues was rather depressing in those days, you know what I mean? There used to be people'd say the Blues was when you was going to -- well, somebody was in trouble. And like, we used to say "Blue Monday", when you had a whole lot of work to do or something like that, we sang the Blues. But on the whole, Atlantic City, they were for more joyous things, you know? And most sob songs and sentimental songs, you know?
